carmen_prodteam: Hey team — tool.call to /tools/shell is returning HTTP 400 with a parse error when our CI runs a deploy. Happens intermittently when the path contains %USERNAME% or when the payload is constructed in the Windows agent shell.

alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body (sanitized) and the SDK/CLI version you used?

carmen_prodteam: Here's a sanitized payload and the curl we used from the Windows CI agent:
```json
{
  "tool": "shell-exec",
  "tool_args": "{\\\"command\\\":\\\"./deploy.sh\\\", \\\"cwd\\\":\\\"C:/Users/%USERNAME%/app\\\", }"
}
```
and the curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  --data-binary $'{"tool":"shell-exec","tool_args":"{\\\"command\\\":\\\"./deploy.sh\\\", \\\"cwd\\\":\\\"C:/Users/%USERNAME%/app\\\", }"}'
```
Note: the Windows CI shells the curl command, so %USERNAME% sometimes expands to an empty string, and we also see ANSI control chars when paths are copied between tools.

alex_support: That tool_args value is a string containing JSON with a trailing comma and unescaped quotes/backslashes — looks like double-encoding + trailing comma. Our logs show: `parse error: unexpected token '}' at offset 94`. Can you share the request_id from the failed call?

carmen_prodteam: request_id: req_8b7f1a2d

jamal_sre: Checked infra logs for req_8b7f1a2d — incoming body had tool_args as a quoted string containing embedded control characters and a trailing comma inside the inner JSON. When %USERNAME% expands to empty, the resulting string can be malformed. Repro locally by running the curl with --data-binary and letting the shell interpolate environment vars; you get the same parse error. Sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] req=req_8b7f1a2d method=POST path=/v1/toolcall status=400 err="parse error: unexpected token '}' at offset 94" body_snippet="...\"tool_args\":\"{\\\\\"command\\\\\":\\\\\"./deploy.sh\\\\\", \\\\\\\"cwd\\\\\":\\\\\"C:/Users//app\\\\\", }\"..."
```

alex_support: Quick workaround — use the official SDK or send a proper JSON object for tool_args instead of a stringified JSON blob. Example (Python SDK):
```python
payload = {
  "tool": "shell-exec",
  "tool_args": {"command": "./deploy.sh", "cwd": "C:/Users/MyUser/app"}
}
client.tool_call(payload)
```
Or with curl (avoid shell expansion by using single-quoted JSON and --data-binary):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \\
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
 --data-binary '{"tool":"shell-exec","tool_args":{"command":"./deploy.sh","cwd":"C:/Users/MyUser/app"}}'
```

incident_bot: Incident created: INC-123456 (priority P1) — tagged @mikaela_runtime @alex_support

mikaela_runtime: Thanks for the repro and request id. Looking at the runtime validator: we currently assume tool_args is either a JSON object or a fully-escaped JSON string without trailing commas or control chars. We should detect common double-encoding patterns and return a clearer diagnostic (e.g., "tool_args appears to be a stringified JSON with syntax errors; try sending an object or properly escaped string"). I'll add a follow-up: - tighten validation error message - add doc snippets for escaping in Windows shells - evaluate a lenient parsing mode behind a feature flag for back-compat. Marking INC-123456 in-progress.

carmen_prodteam: Confirmed — switching to the SDK fixed our pipeline immediately. Please keep me updated on a permanent fix. Thanks!
